I have not added sustainability yet, because I do not know what it means for this decision or why you care. Repair policy and spare parts already cover how long a kettle stays usable, so it may overlap them.

What does sustainability mean here (energy use, materials, or something else), and what decision will it feed?

I have not added a column, because this is already covered: the spare-parts criterion asks for how long the maker states it stocks spare parts.

Two kettles identical except for how many years the maker keeps parts in stock: do you prefer one, or are you indifferent? If you are indifferent it is not a new column. If you are not, tell me the reason and I will use it as an exclusion that keeps the two apart.

This would change the repair-policy criterion rather than add one, so I have not edited it. Cells already recorded under repair-policy would answer the older definition and need re-scoring. So far the analysis has one scored cell and one settled blank in total.

Do you want repair-policy to count the heating element, so that a policy excluding it scores as bad?

I have not added energy use per boil as a column. You count kitchen electricity in the sustainability report, so energy per boil matters only as a way of meeting that sustainability objective. That makes it a means, not a criterion of its own.

Do you want sustainability as the criterion, with energy per boil as how it is measured, or is energy per boil a veto (a kettle over some level is out)? Lower is better, as you said, and the makers' watt-hours per litre would be the evidence.
